summary.text: Mir was a space station operated in low Earth orbit from 1986 to 2001, first by the Soviet Union and later by the Russian Federation.
It was the first modular space station, assembled in orbit from 1986 to 1996, and the first continuously inhabited long-term research station in orbit.
Crews did experiments in biology, physics, astronomy and more, aiming to develop technologies needed for permanent occupation of space.

facts.label: Longest flight
facts.value: Valeri Polyakov spent 437 days aboard, 1994 to 1995

facts.label: Modules
facts.value: Seven pressurised modules plus unpressurised parts

facts.label: Orbit
facts.value: 296 to 421 km high, 15.7 orbits per day

items.prompt: Mir's first section went up in 1986 and more sections were added in orbit until 1996. What kind of station did that make it?

options.label: The first space station ever launched
The first station occupied by a crew
The first modular space station
The first station with docking ports

items.explain: Mir was the first modular space station, assembled in orbit from 1986 to 1996. Salyut 1 was the first station overall.

items.prompt: A cosmonaut lived aboard Mir for 437 days. What does that record measure?

options.label: The longest single human spaceflight
The longest continuous presence of people on any station
The most spacewalks by one person
The most visitors in a single year

items.explain: Valeri Polyakov holds the record for the longest single human spaceflight. The station's own 3,644 days of continuous presence is a different record.

items.prompt: Nearly every part of Mir went up on Proton rockets. Which piece arrived another way?

options.label: The Core Module, launched in 1986
Kvant-1, delivered by a space tug
The photovoltaic arrays on the modules
The Docking Module, installed by the Shuttle

items.explain: Proton rockets launched all components except the Docking Module, which the Space Shuttle installed on STS-74.

items.prompt: Most of Mir's occupants were Soviet or Russian. How did travellers from Asia, Europe and North America get aboard?

options.label: By buying tickets on commercial tourist flights
Through international programs such as Interkosmos, Euromir and Shuttle–Mir
Through the Salyut programme that Mir replaced
They only watched from separate craft

items.explain: International collaborations such as the Interkosmos, Euromir and Shuttle–Mir programmes made the station accessible to travellers from several nations.

items.prompt: When it was authorised in 1976, what was Mir meant to be?

options.label: An improved model of the Salyut space stations
A copy of the American Skylab
A ferry craft for Soyuz crews
A base on the Moon

items.explain: Mir was authorised to design an improved model of the Salyut space stations.

items.prompt: Mir's core module had a docking sphere with several ports at the front. What was that for?

options.label: So it could spin to create artificial gravity
So crews could sleep in separate compartments
So more modules could join and expand what the station could do
So Soyuz ferries could refuel quickly

items.explain: The ports were planned to allow more modules to expand the station's capabilities.
